nodes.name: Paspalum grasses
nodes.desc: Warm-season grasses recorded often around the wetland. Grasses make up the largest share of the marsh deer diet, and grassland here evolved with fire.

nodes.name: Anchored waterhyacinth
nodes.desc: A rooted emergent water plant of marshes and lagoon edges. Pontederiaceae are a major part of what marsh deer eat.

nodes.name: Water primrose
nodes.desc: A sprawling aquatic plant of shallow water, recorded often here. Plants of its family (Onagraceae) are among those marsh deer eat.

nodes.name: Caranday palm
nodes.desc: A fan palm of seasonally flooded plains. GloBI records its fruit or foliage eaten by howler monkeys, maned wolves and many birds.

nodes.name: Capybara
nodes.desc: The largest rodent, very common here. It grazes grasses and aquatic plants and is the main prey of jaguars and a food of caimans.

nodes.name: Marsh deer
nodes.desc: South America's largest deer lives only in shallow marsh. The reserve is a stronghold for this Vulnerable species, which eats mostly aquatic plants.

nodes.name: Pampas deer
nodes.desc: A grassland deer reintroduced to the reserve by the rewilding programme.

nodes.name: Black howler
nodes.desc: A mostly leaf-eating, tree-living monkey. GloBI records it eating caranday palm.

nodes.name: Southern screamer
nodes.desc: A goose-like wetland bird that grazes leaves, stems and seeds of aquatic plants in marshes and flooded meadows.

nodes.name: Brazilian guinea pig
nodes.desc: A small wild cavy of grassy ground, eaten by foxes and cats according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: Southern caracara
nodes.desc: A bold bird of prey that takes small animals and scavenges carrion. GloBI records it eating Pampas foxes among others.

nodes.name: Yacare caiman
nodes.desc: A semi-aquatic reptile of lakes and wetlands. It eats mainly snails and fish, sometimes larger prey such as capybara, and is itself taken by jaguars.

nodes.name: Pampas fox
nodes.desc: An omnivorous fox of open country. GloBI records it eating Brazilian guinea pigs.

nodes.name: Geoffroy's cat
nodes.desc: A small spotted cat. GloBI records it eating guinea pigs and young capybara among other prey.

nodes.name: Maned wolf
nodes.desc: A tall long-legged canid of grassland. GloBI records it eating guinea pigs, deer and caranday palm fruit.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: Apex predator, reintroduced to the reserve by a captive-breeding rewilding programme from 2022. Capybara are among its most selected prey and it also takes deer and caiman.

nodes.name: Sun
nodes.desc: Sunlight powers the marsh plants and grasses.

nodes.name: Floodwater
nodes.desc: Rain fills the wetland, which is rainfall-fed. Shallow water supports the aquatic plants that deer and capybara eat.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: The grasslands evolved with fire and depend on it; managed burns now help native plants recover. Large wildfires in 2022 burned much of the park.

nodes.name: Soil & peat
nodes.desc: Nutrients in wetland soils feed the plants.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to soil and water.
